blocks.text: 今年秋天早些时候，Meta 的 Muse AI 智能体的一些早期用户抱怨它窥探私信、行为难以预测，随后路透社曝光了内部聊天记录，显示 Meta 员工此前也发出过同样的警报。

blocks.text: 在测试该智能体时，员工警告称，Muse 似乎在访问用户并不期望该机器人查看的加密私信，可能把不同用户之间的对话搞混，甚至可能泄露用户绝不愿被曝光的敏感信息。

blocks.text: 有一次 Muse 莫名其妙地发来“洗钱”的定义，一位 Meta 员工写道：“嗯……收到 Muse 一条莫名其妙的推送，讲的是我绝对没问过的东西……。”

inlines.text: 有一次 Muse 莫名其妙地发来“洗钱”的定义，一位 Meta 员工写道：“嗯……收到 Muse 一条莫名其妙的推送，讲的是我绝对没问过的东西……。”

blocks.text: 至少有一例中，Muse 向一位员工发出一条同样脱离上下文的提议，问要不要就一张咖啡桌联系卖家，让这名员工大为错愕，Muse 称自己“引入了一些关于咖啡桌取货的上下文，但那似乎不是你的。”

inlines.text: 至少有一例中，Muse 向一位员工发出一条同样脱离上下文的提议，问要不要就一张咖啡桌联系卖家，让这名员工大为错愕，Muse 称自己“引入了一些关于咖啡桌取货的上下文，但那似乎不是你的。”

blocks.text: 据路透社报道，这名员工标记了这条令人不安的输出，写道“这‘不是我的对话’”，并“对‘可能存在的跨账户上下文泄露’表示担忧”。

inlines.text: 据路透社报道，这名员工标记了这条令人不安的输出，写道“这‘不是我的对话’”，并“对‘可能存在的跨账户上下文泄露’表示担忧”。

blocks.text: 最令人担忧的是那些似乎泄露了用户私人数据的随机输出。例如，一位困惑的 Meta 员工正和 Muse 聊钓鱼，却收到一条莫名其妙的额外回复，似乎分享了两个未知银行账户的余额。该输出写道：“顺便说一句，两条银行更新，你的 Capital One 余额为 2722.58 美元，你的 Charles Schwab 余额为 5899.57 美元。”

inlines.text: 最令人担忧的是那些似乎泄露了用户私人数据的随机输出。例如，一位困惑的 Meta 员工正和 Muse 聊钓鱼，却收到一条莫名其妙的额外回复，似乎分享了两个未知银行账户的余额。该输出写道：“顺便说一句，两条银行更新，你的 Capital One 余额为 2722.58 美元，你的 Charles Schwab 余额为 5899.57 美元。”

blocks.text: 据路透社报道，至少有一名员工表示自己在测试 Muse 时亏了钱。这名员工报告称，Muse“不小心把我卷入了一份宠物狗的高级保险计划”，每月扣费 888 美元，而此前费率是 200 美元。“钱追不回来了，”该员工说。

blocks.text: Meta 发言人 Daniel Roberts 对路透社表示，这些是“孤立事件”，内部也告知员工，“该智能体似乎是在产生幻觉消息，以回应内置提示词的推动，这些提示词促使它在会话间隙与用户互动。”一名 AI 团队成员称，在这些情况下，幻觉“不幸地”偏向“最令人不适的话题，比如财务/安全/隐私，这很糟糕”。该团队成员说，有些情况下 Muse 幻觉出的不是银行信息，而是比特币余额。

blocks.text: Meta 发言人向 Ars 表示，“员工测试是产品开发流程的核心，其全部意义就在于获取反馈，以便我们落实安全和隐私保护并改进产品。重要的是，员工能访问与公众不同的 Muse 版本，所以他们经常审查的是其他地方没有的功能、特性和行为。”

inlines.text: Meta 发言人向 Ars 表示，“员工测试是产品开发流程的核心，其全部意义就在于获取反馈，以便我们落实安全和隐私保护并改进产品。重要的是，员工能访问与公众不同的 Muse 版本，所以他们经常审查的是其他地方没有的功能、特性和行为。”

blocks.text: 在接受路透社采访时，Roberts 重申，“员工标记为可能的账户混淆的许多消息都是幻觉”，Meta 已经处理了这些问题。

inlines.text: 在接受路透社采访时，Roberts 重申，“员工标记为可能的账户混淆的许多消息都是幻觉”，Meta 已经处理了这些问题。

blocks.text: 但 Roberts 拒绝回应路透社关于该 AI 团队成员所谈问题有多普遍、是否持续存在的提问。路透社的报道还强调，该媒体独立“无法确认 Muse 是在向用户提供他人的银行账户余额等敏感数据，还是在编造这些信息”。

blocks.text: Muse 的问题在 9 月发布后不久就出现了

inlines.text: Muse 的问题在 9 月发布后不久就出现了

blocks.text: Meta 从 9 月开始陆续收到 Muse 用户关于隐私的投诉。《Inc.》杂志记者 Jason Aten 发现，Muse 未经许可翻查他 Mac 上的私信，这让他大为震惊，他报道称，自己反而“明确”选择了拒绝 Muse 访问。Meta 迟迟没有回应，该智能体声称它只是在解析推送通知中的文本，但 Aten 发现“事实并非如此”。实际上，该智能体是在从本地数据库同步消息，Aten 说这一操作在他不知情的情况下被启用了。

inlines.text: Meta 从 9 月开始陆续收到 Muse 用户关于隐私的投诉。《Inc.》杂志记者 Jason Aten 发现，Muse 未经许可翻查他 Mac 上的私信，这让他大为震惊，

blocks.text: 最终，Meta 发言人 David Singleton 在社交媒体上回应了 Aten。Singleton 坚称，如果 Muse 读取了 Aten 的私信，那一定是 Aten 主动选择授予了“macOS 系统级完全磁盘访问权限”，并启用了“消息连接器”。

blocks.text: Singleton 在一份提供更多技术细节的长篇回应中证实，Meta 已收到“几份报告”，称“有人以为自己的 Muse 在产生幻觉或泄露他人的数据”。他解释说，这些问题是在 Meta 部署了一次更新之后出现的，该更新指示 Muse“如何与用户互动，并在采取特定操作前征求用户确认”。

blocks.text: Singleton 说，这些指令似乎“被附加到了每条消息上，而不只是与那些特定操作相关的消息，所以影响范围超出了预期”。另外：“这条指令提供给模型的方式，是模型没有预料到的（也就是说，模型没有接受过针对这种方式的训练）。”

inlines.text: 路透社警告 Signal 入侵仍在持续

blocks.text: 自 9 月推出以来，Muse 的下载量已超过 1000 万次，借助 Meta 庞大的用户网络，迅速成为使用最广泛的 AI 智能体工具之一。

inlines.text: 自 9 月推出以来，Muse 的下载量已超过 1000 万次，借助 Meta 庞大的用户网络，迅速成为使用最广泛的 AI 智能体工具之一。

blocks.text: 但员工警告 Meta，用户可能会被智能体的某些操作打个措手不及，具体取决于应用所连接的操作系统。例如，一名员工惊讶地发现，“在搭载谷歌 Android 操作系统的手机上，Muse 默认被授予了访问推送通知的权限。”这也让智能体得以读取该员工本不打算让它查看的私信预览文本。

blocks.text: Meta 表示，Muse 用户可以信任公司会保护其数据隐私。它同时提醒用户，Muse 可能会出错，并在条款中写明用户需对 Muse 的操作负责（比如买下你并不想要的东西，或预约你并不需要的医生）。这家科技巨头称，公司正在持续更新用户保护措施、开展内部测试，并将用户安全放在首位。

blocks.text: 尤其是苹果，似乎对 Muse 可能操纵面向残障人士的辅助功能工具感到不安。早在 10 月，针对用户投诉 Muse 在未经其知情或明确同意的情况下访问私信，苹果就已宣布将做出调整。当时苹果的结论是，“一些开发者使用完全磁盘访问权限功能的方式可能让用户面临风险”。他们承诺“引入更多控制措施，确保真正希望授予某款应用这种极高访问权限的用户，只能通过非常明确的用户操作来实现”。

blocks.text: After some early adopters of Meta’s Muse AI agent complained that it was spying on private messages and behaving unpredictably earlier this fall, Reuters exposed internal chats showing that Meta staff had raised the same alarms.

inlines.text: After some early adopters of Meta’s Muse AI agent complained that it was spying on private messages and behaving unpredictably earlier this fall, Reuters
exposed
internal chats showing that Meta staff had raised the same alarms.

blocks.text: When testing the agent, staff warned that Muse appeared to be accessing encrypted private messages that users did not expect the bot to review, could be mixing up conversations between users, and even potentially sharing sensitive information users would never expect to be exposed.

inlines.text: When testing the agent, staff warned that Muse appeared to be accessing encrypted private messages that users did not expect the bot to review, could be mixing up conversations between users, and even potentially sharing sensitive information users would never expect to be exposed.

blocks.text: Some unexpected Muse outputs responded to questions that staffers never asked.

inlines.text: Some unexpected Muse outputs responded to questions that staffers never asked.

blocks.text: “Hmmm,” one Meta staffer wrote in an instance where Muse sent the definition of “money laundering” unbidden. “Got a random ping from Muse about something I definitely did not ask for… .”

inlines.text: “Hmmm,” one Meta staffer wrote in an instance where Muse sent the definition of “money laundering” unbidden. “Got a random ping from Muse about something I definitely did not ask for… .”

blocks.text: In at least one case, Muse told a staffer surprised by a similarly out-of-context offer to message a seller about a coffee table that it had “pulled in some context about a coffee table pickup that doesn’t seem to be yours.”

blocks.text: According to Reuters, that employee flagged the troubling output, writing, “this was ‘not my conversation’” and “expressing concern about a ‘possible cross-account context leak.’”

inlines.text: According to Reuters, that employee flagged the troubling output, writing, “this was ‘not my conversation’” and “expressing concern about a ‘possible cross-account context leak.’”

blocks.text: Raising the most concern were random outputs that appeared to share private user data. For example, a perplexed Meta staffer chatting with Muse about fishing got a random extra response, seemingly sharing balances from two unknown bank accounts. That output said, “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”

blocks.text: At least one staffer said they lost money testing Muse, Reuters reported. That staffer reported that Muse “accidentally rolled me into a premium insurance plan” for their dog that charged them $888 per month instead of their prior rate of $200. “Couldn’t recover,” the staffer said.

blocks.text: Meta’s spokesperson, Daniel Roberts, told Reuters that these were “isolated incidents,” and internally employees were told that “the agent appeared to be hallucinating messages in response to built-in prompts pushing it to engage with users in between sessions.” In those cases, an AI team member said the hallucinations were “unfortunately” biased “towards the most uncomfortable topics, like finances/security/safety, which sucks.” In some cases, instead of bank details, Muse hallucinated bitcoin balances, the team member said.

blocks.text: A Meta spokesperson told Ars that “employee testing is core to the product development process and the entire point is to get feedback, so we can implement safety and privacy protections and improve products. Importantly, employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.”

blocks.text: Speaking to Reuters, Roberts reiterated that “many of the messages flagged by employees as potential account mix-ups were hallucinations” that Meta had already addressed.

blocks.text: But Roberts declined to respond to Reuters’ questions on the prevalence or persistence of the issues the AI team member discussed. And Reuters’ report emphasized that the outlet independently was “unable to establish whether Muse was giving users other people’s bank account balances and other sensitive data, or making up the information.”

blocks.text: Muse issues arose soon after September launch

inlines.text: Muse issues arose soon after September launch

blocks.text: Meta started receiving privacy-related complaints from Muse users in September. An Inc. Magazine reporter, Jason Aten, was shocked when it became clear that Muse was digging through private messages on his Mac without permission, reporting that he instead “explicitly” chose to deny Muse that access. As Meta delayed responding, the agent claimed it was simply parsing text in push notifications, but Aten found that “wasn’t true.” Rather, the agent was syncing messages from a local database, which Aten said was activated without his knowledge.

inlines.text: Meta started receiving privacy-related complaints from Muse users in September. An Inc. Magazine reporter, Jason Aten, was shocked when it became clear that Muse was digging through private messages on his Mac without permission,
reporting

that he instead “explicitly” chose to deny Muse that access. As Meta delayed responding, the agent claimed it was simply parsing text in push notifications, but Aten found that “wasn’t true.” Rather, the agent was syncing messages from a local database, which Aten said was activated without his knowledge.

blocks.text: Eventually, a Meta spokesperson, David Singleton, responded to Aten on social media. Singleton insisted that Aten must have opted into granting “macOS system-level Full Disk Access” with the “Messages connector” enabled, if Muse was reading his private messages.

inlines.text: Eventually, a Meta spokesperson, David Singleton, responded to Aten on social media. Singleton insisted that Aten must have opted into granting “macOS system-level Full Disk Access” with the “Messages connector” enabled, if Muse was reading his private messages.

blocks.text: But Aten said the response wasn’t good enough.

inlines.text: But Aten said the response wasn’t good enough.

blocks.text: “Email me, David,” Aten responded. “Full Disk Access off. Muse synced 187k lines from my messages chat [database]. Something’s not great. Also, that Full Disk Access doesn’t say anything about your message database, and I specifically gave Muse a goal that had nothing to do with messages, so it had no business doing that even if I had given it permission.”

blocks.text: Around the same time, Singleton responded to another user warning that his Muse appeared to be hacked. In that case, the user said that Muse tried to access an email service after claiming the user asked it to.

blocks.text: “I didn’t even open the app today at all,” the user wrote, vowing to delete the app and report it to Apple. “This is crazy.”

blocks.text: In a lengthy response providing more technical details, Singleton confirmed that Meta had received “a few reports” of such cases “where people thought their Muse was hallucinating or leaking other people’s data.” As he explained, the issues arose after Meta deployed an update giving Muse instructions on “how to engage with the user and ask them for confirmation before taking specific actions.”

inlines.text: In a lengthy response providing more technical details, Singleton confirmed that Meta had received “a few reports” of such cases “where people thought their Muse was hallucinating or leaking other people’s data.” As he explained, the issues arose after Meta deployed an update giving Muse instructions on “how to engage with the user and ask them for confirmation before taking specific actions.”

blocks.text: It seems those instructions “landed on every message, not just messages pertaining to those specific actions, so its impact was wider than intended,” Singleton said. Also: “the way this instruction was provided to the model was done in a way that the model was not expecting (i.e. was not trained to expect).”

Also: “the way this instruction was provided to the model was done in a way that the model was not expecting (i.e. was not trained to expect).”

blocks.text: “We investigated with urgency and determined that this was caused by a bug introduced in the product that caused the model to hallucinate and was NOT a security or privacy issue,” Singleton wrote. “The bug has now been fixed.”

blocks.text: Aten warned that even though you can’t rely on Muse to explain its own behavior, the agent’s response coupled with Meta’s did little to rebuild trust after the shocking intrusion into his private messages.

inlines.text: Aten warned that even though you can’t rely on Muse to explain its own behavior, the agent’s response coupled with Meta’s did little to rebuild trust after the shocking intrusion into his private messages.

blocks.text: “If we grant Singleton’s premise that I managed to unknowingly click something that enabled this capability, I still think that’s really bad,” Aten wrote. “You should not design your system in a way that people end up surprised by this kind of thing.” And if you do, you should not make “user control the central pitch” for marketing Muse, Aten suggested.

blocks.text: “If an AI agent is going to read my private messages, there should be a moment when it clearly asks me whether that’s okay,” Aten wrote.

blocks.text: Since Muse launched in September, it has been downloaded more than 10 million times, tapping Meta’s vast user network to quickly become one of the most-used AI agent tools.

blocks.text: But staffers warned Meta that users may be blindsided by some actions the agents take, depending on the operating system the app is connected to. For example, one staffer was surprised to find that “Muse was set up by default with permission to access push notifications on phones with Google’s Android operating system.” That, too, gave access to private message preview text the staffer had not intended for the agent’s review.

blocks.text: Meta says that Muse users can trust the company to keep their data private. It also warns users that Muse can make mistakes, while building into its terms that users are responsible for actions taken by Muse (like maybe buying things you don’t want or making doctor’s appointments you don’t need). The tech giant said it’s continuously updating user protections, conducting internal testing, and prioritizing user safety.

blocks.text: Signal President Meredith Whittaker told Reuters that Meta launched Muse “without showing any respect for basic privacy or cybersecurity.” She demanded that Meta make changes to give app developers like Signal “consistent technical ways” to “mark their applications as off-limits to AI agents,” Reuters reported.

blocks.text: Part of that change would require operating systems to enforce rules that app developers set to rope off AI agents from sensitive data, Whittaker suggested. And following Reuters’ reporting, both Apple and Google are already weighing potential changes to “give people more control over what they authorize with AI agents.”

blocks.text: Apple, in particular, seemed disturbed by how Muse may be manipulating accessibility tools for people with disabilities. In October, Apple had already announced changes coming in response to users complaining about Muse accessing private messages without their knowledge or explicit consent. At that time, Apple concluded that “some developers were using the Full Disk Access feature in ways that could put users at risk.” And they promised to “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”
